notes: Word.Html and Markdown.Html bring OfficeIMO.Html + AngleSharp; include them so the front door keeps HTML import and Markdown raw-HTML fidelity (Word.Markdown no longer references Word.Html).
Reader.All brings 31 reader handlers; confirm that is wanted (the design lists "Reader" without scope).
Workflows is not referenced: it brings Invoicing, Project, OCR, Visio, DjVu, CHM, EPUB, Email and is net8/net10 only.

publicTypes: OfficeConverter (static): Convert(string source, string destination, OfficeConversionOptions options = null) : OfficeConversionReport; Convert(Stream source, OfficeFormat sourceFormat, Stream destination, OfficeFormat target, OfficeConversionOptions options = null); ConvertAsync(...) twins; ConvertAsync(IEnumerable<string> sources, string outputDirectory, OfficeFormat target, OfficeBatchOptions options = null) : Task<OfficeBatchReport>; Analyze(string source, string destination, OfficeConversionOptions options = null) : OfficeConversionReport (proposed); Register(IOfficeConversionRoute route) (proposed, for Tier 2 routes)

OfficeFormat (enum): Docx, Doc, Dotx, Docm, Xlsx, Xls, Xlsb, Xlsm, Pptx, Ppt, Pdf, Md, Html, Png, Jpeg, Svg, Tiff, Webp, ... (one value per file format; Core already has OfficeDocumentFormat - see openQuestions)

OfficeConversionOptions: target-specific option bags (Word = WordPdfExportOptions, ...), FailOnLoss, conflict policy, limits; replaces OfficeWorkflowConversionOptions and Word/Excel/PowerPoint *DocumentConversionOptions

OfficeBatchOptions: MaxParallelism, ResumeFrom, OutputDirectory, Recursive, Extensions, ConflictPolicy, limits, Load/Save (JSON job file); replaces OfficeConversionJob, OfficeConversionBatchRequest and builder state
OfficeBatchReport / OfficeBatchItemReport: per-item OfficeConversionReport, totals, elapsed, resume state; replaces OfficeConversionBatchResult/Report and OfficeConversionJobRunReport
OfficeDocument (static): Inspect(string path, OfficeInspectOptions options = null) for any format (design: Lifecycle)
absorbs: OfficeIMO.Workflows Batches/ and ConversionJobs/ (checkpointing, resume, publication guard) - port to netstandard2.0
*ToPdfBytes helpers in Word, PowerPoint, Excel.Pdf (and Tier 2 *.Pdf adapters: 400 files call ToPdfBytes, mostly tests)

conflicts: OfficeIMO.Core already declares 101 public types in the OfficeIMO namespace (OfficeConversionResult<,>, OfficeOutputResult<>, OfficeDocumentFormat, OfficeDocumentModel, OfficePageOrientation, OfficeConversionLossPolicy, IOfficeConversionReport, ...). The rule "the OfficeIMO namespace holds only OfficeConverter, OfficeFormat and the batch types" conflicts with Core unless Core moves to OfficeIMO.Core (a repo-wide break) or the rule is relaxed to "OfficeIMO namespace = Core shared types + the converter".
OfficeColor and the drawing types live in OfficeIMO.Drawing (374 Core types), not OfficeIMO.
OfficeDocumentFormat (Core) and the planned OfficeFormat overlap; keep one.
openQuestions: OfficeIMO.Core already places 101 public types in the OfficeIMO namespace; see OfficeIMO.json conflicts.

Dropping the Windows-only net472 TFM means .NET Framework consumers run the netstandard2.0 build. #if NETFRAMEWORK workarounds (Word Save snapshot, Excel non-seekable stream save, PDF NET472 branches) must become runtime checks, and the netstandard2.0 build must be tested on .NET Framework 4.7.2 (PSWriteOffice on Windows PowerShell 5.1 is the main consumer).

Static From{Source} on a type owned by another package (WordDocument.FromHtml in OfficeIMO.Word.Html, WordDocument.FromMarkdown, MarkdownDocument.FromHtml, WordDocument.FromPdf) is only possible with C# 14 static extension members. The SDK supports them for netstandard2.0 targets, but callers on older language versions (.NET Framework projects default to C# 7.3, Windows PowerShell) must call the containing static class directly. Alternative: keep instance forms on the source (pdf.ToWord(), html.ToWordDocument()) as the only adapter shape.

C# forbids out parameters on async methods, so "To{Target}/From{Source} have an overload with out OfficeConversionReport" cannot cover the async forms (FromHtmlAsync, LoadResultAsync, ToWordDocumentResultAsync). Choose: async forms return a (TDocument, OfficeConversionReport) result type, or async forms only throw/ignore loss.

Package IDs OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf and OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf flip direction (PDF->Word reconstruction today, Word->PDF export after). Same NuGet ID with an unrelated API is a silent break for anyone pinning 3.5.x; MIGRATION.md and the release notes must say so explicitly, or the export adapters take new IDs.

Word image export is built on the PDF writer+reader+renderer (WordPageImageExport). Keeping image export in OfficeIMO.Word without the PDF engine requires splitting OfficeIMO.Pdf into a composition/pagination core that paints to OfficeIMO.Drawing (Core) and a PDF writer. That is a large engine refactor; the cheaper option is to move Word image export to OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf (or a new OfficeIMO.Word.Imaging that references Pdf) and accept that Word image export needs the PDF engine. PowerPoint does not have this problem (its scene renderer already targets OfficeIMO.Drawing).

designResolutions.frontDoorTarget: OfficeIMO, its batch engine, OfficeIMO.Workflows and OfficeIMO.Workflows.IWork target netstandard2.0, net8.0 and net10.0, plus net472 through the existing Windows-only project condition (approved c526a10ad2). phaseA.scope: Package boundaries, target frameworks, lifecycle, options, conversions and names.

extraChanges.subject: Front-door native conversion
extraChanges.note: File/stream conversion captures bounded input, retains existing native compatibility/carrier/fallback owners and atomically publishes after source verification and host checks. Batch execution and complete consumer migration remain in progress.

extraChanges.subject: PDF HTML adapter reference
extraChanges.note: The front door also references the existing OfficeIMO.Html.Pdf adapter to retain the currently executable PDF-to-HTML route. This is an existing first-party owner, with no new external runtime dependency.

extraChanges.subject: Shared orchestration policy owners
extraChanges.note: OfficePublicationPolicy (Fail/Replace/Rename), OfficeConversionProfile and OfficeOperationLimits move from Workflows into Core/root namespace. The two-value native OfficeConversionFileConflictPolicy keeps its exact-destination role; Rename belongs to orchestration, whose report returns the actual output path.

extraChanges.subject: Batch and saved-definition ownership
extraChanges.note: The existing durable batch executor, bounded report collection, saved job persistence, runtime secret references, report leases, retention and interrupted-attempt inspection move to the OfficeIMO front door. OfficeBatchOptions and OfficeBatchReport absorb the old public batch/job/run types. Private execution DTOs prevent a dependency on Workflows.

extraChanges.subject: ResumeFrom manifest placement
extraChanges.note: The approved design uses ResumeFrom as a JSON manifest inside output. Private receipts and a lease live in ResumeFrom + .state; source and output remain separate. Hash-verified pending publication intent is retained before final moves. No old checkpoint is silently replaced.

extraChanges.subject: Saved batch schema
extraChanges.note: New saved definitions and reports use v2 schemas. Unsupported saved definitions are rejected explicitly. Portable scalar settings and environment-variable secret references are retained; advanced renderer instances and callbacks remain runtime-only and cannot be silently serialized.

extraChanges.subject: Checkpoint route qualification
extraChanges.note: Existing native renderer routes retain checkpoint support. New callback-rich import/Reader routes currently run ordinary batches; they require deterministic provider/configuration identity before durable reuse can be qualified. Trusted first-party registrations supply a private configuration fingerprint hook; arbitrary external registrations are ordinary-batch only.

extraChanges.subject: Native route discovery
extraChanges.note: Native Word, Excel and PowerPoint variant conversion and XLS/XLSB/PPT-to-PDF routes join the canonical Core catalog. Existing DOCX/XLSX/PPTX routes admit supported template/macro variants. Source codecs retain preservation/carrier/encryption behavior; unsupported destination generations are rejected by their owner.

extraChanges.subject: Canonical resource and publication helpers
extraChanges.note: HTML resource resolution and guarded file publication move from Workflows to the front door. Resources remain scoped to captured sources, and publication preserves Fail/Replace/Rename race checks and host guards.

extraChanges.subject: Reading and validation ownership
extraChanges.note: The former Reader.All PDF facade moves into OfficeConverter. Registered artifacts are reopened before publication. PDF input snapshots apply SourcePassword and the operation byte cap as well as PdfLoadOptions.

extraChanges.subject: Batch diagnostic codes
extraChanges.note: conversion-failed, conversion-input-skipped and recorded-diagnostics-truncated are emitted through the shared M1 catalog. Shared reports use a private source-generated persistence DTO, preserving Core without a JSON dependency.

extraChanges.subject: Cross-framework batch execution
extraChanges.note: The front door and all its dependencies retain their original framework reach. Internal Core runtime helpers use modern APIs behind framework guards and bounded fallbacks for hashes, relative paths, byte streams and parallel conversion. Compiler markers remain internal to each older-framework assembly.

extraChanges.subject: Legacy graph validation
extraChanges.note: OfficeIMOCompatibilityTarget=netstandard2.0 selects the entire library dependency graph for runtime tests on a modern host. Normal framework declarations and platform-specific locks are unchanged. This is additional runtime proof; Windows .NET Framework and PowerShell 5.1 execution remain required.

extraChanges.subject: Native staging and analysis
extraChanges.note: Native Analyze invokes the existing assessment kernels without serializing a target and reports zero written items. Private source and target directories remain separate. Same-format routes remain excluded because the owning native converters require different concrete formats.

extraChanges.subject: Format-neutral inspection owner
extraChanges.note: OfficeDocument.Inspect returns OfficeDocumentInfo with optional Reader content and selected native security, provenance, signature and PDF preflight reports. Path and bounded caller-owned stream overloads reuse existing inspection kernels; IncludeContent=false skips Reader extraction.

extraChanges.subject: Modern analyzer coverage
extraChanges.note: Directory.Build.targets enables the existing SDK trimming and NativeAOT analyzers for modern packable library builds, including net8.0. No new runtime dependency is added. Analyzer qualification and AOT smoke execution remain in progress.

extraChanges.subject: Theme-role AOT enumeration
extraChanges.note: Theme-role parsing in OfficeColor uses the existing internal EnumCompat generic path on modern targets instead of Enum.GetValues(Type), closing IL3050 under the restored net8.0 AOT analyzer. Core net8.0 builds with zero warnings and errors.

extraChanges.subject: Retained portable workflow policies
extraChanges.note: OfficeConversionOptions retains compression as CompressPdfOutput. WordLoadOptions.FailOnLoss controls legacy Word import loss. OfficeBatchOptions keeps separate native/PDF environment-secret references; format-owned password settings take precedence. PDF compression precedes final encryption. CLI checkpoint-folder flags select plan.json inside that folder. Retry, report delivery and AllowEmpty remain admitted run overrides.

extraChanges.subject: Completed conversion ownership and consumer grammar
extraChanges.note: OfficeConversionOptions exposes Clone for independent public consumer settings. Word source loss acceptance uses WordLoadOptions.FailOnLoss rather than a separate legacy-loss policy. Shared PDF compression staging is reused internally by Workflows. Studio and the CLI persist OfficeBatchOptions and read flattened OfficeBatchReport; PSWriteOffice retains existing command and parameter names while calling those owners.

extraChanges.change: Input capture uses a bounded buffer with an input-specific failure. Output limits retain the existing shared marker, so consumers can distinguish source budget rejection from output budget rejection.
extraChanges.reason: The common bounded memory buffer otherwise classifies every capacity failure as output, including while capturing an input.

extraChanges.note: PdfOcrMergeResult source extensions reconstruct Word, Excel and PowerPoint through the existing reverse adapter kernels, preserving recognized words and tables without serializing and re-reading OCR output. The front door references the first-party Pdf.Ocr owner; format and reconstruction adapter dependencies stay isolated.

Specialized static content-safety, provenance and signature inspection entry points are internal native kernels. OfficeDocument.Inspect(path, OfficeInspectOptions) returns OfficeDocumentInfo with selectable typed reports and optional native content. IncludeContent=false preserves inspection without content extraction; original package/signature/provenance guards and explicit provider selection remain in their owning libraries. Provenance takes an independent options snapshot with caller cancellation.

Async conversion entry points capture options before deferred work or resource awaits. The same snapshot supplies resource/size limits and final FailOnLoss acceptance; caller-owned template documents and callbacks retain their ownership.

Strict adapter PDF saves use the existing staged writer with shared report acceptance before publication. Source-stage and writer-time losses throw OfficeConversionException carrying OfficeConversionReport; native advanced result policies keep their existing behavior. The same writer and file/stream publication owners are reused. Front-door HTML/TXT saves dispose the generated model.

Normalized Reader content exposes ToPdf/out-report/ToPdfAsync and shared SaveAsPdf forms from the front door. PdfProjectionOptions snapshots FailOnLoss; native Reader-to-neutral projection stays internal. Reader package dependencies remain unchanged. Saved sample jobs and workflow README examples use the shared v2 batch contract.

Internal diagnostic comparisons, report counters, typed adapter forwarding, test expectations and machine-generated report/visual fixtures consume the same M1 code values as emission sites. Native feature names, severity, location and loss classifications remain independent. PSWriteOffice retains its command names, concurrency parameters and saved-job error IDs while returning the shared conversion report.

Reader Email, Epub and Visio grant the front door internal access to their options snapshot owners. OfficeConversionOptions.Clone stays portable when default Reader settings were never requested, and applies Reader defaults only at the execution boundary. Portable settings validate bounded encoding names before Studio starts a batch.

Checkpointed batch item reports identify the final published output path; private staging names do not appear as OfficeConversionReport.OutputPath. Failure and cancellation reports have no published path. The saved report round trip verifies the same contract.

PDF reconstruction forwards the captured PDF read settings to each adapter, including selected visual Word pages. HTML file conversion admits local resources only through the bounded, contained resolver. Source import reports survive a later PDF output failure. Checkpoint item reports expose the final output path, including saved report JSON. PDF-to-HTML rendering receives the output character budget before constructing its complete HTML string.

Registered route checkpoint fingerprints include XML source acceptance, so lowering the XML budget cannot reuse an earlier accepted artifact. PDF compression evidence is recorded before deferred encryption and retained if encryption exceeds the output budget. HTML rendering shares one input budget with relative resources.

Cross-format and registered editable outputs honor native destination save options, including passwords. File and stream publication retain completed reports on failure. Analysis discards staged sidecars; publication guards and conflict policy apply to each sidecar before acceptance.

Normal Reader, image and RTF PDF save paths now use the same guarded final-output owner as strict saves. Completed source diagnostics survive file/stream failures; destination arguments are validated before conversion.

InternalsVisibleTo grants the existing browser engine and its tests access to detailed conversion and serialization evidence. This preserves browser diagnostics while keeping conversion kernels outside the public API.
ConfigureMarkdownHtml is internal and reused by the browser Markdown-to-Word route to preserve the canonical raw-HTML hook without duplicating HTML rendering.
